question.text: At the start of the day, open interest in 10-year GOI bond futures is 5,000 lots. During the day: Trader A buys 100 lots (new), Trader B sells 100 lots (new), Trader C sells 50 lots to close, and Trader D buys 50 lots (new). What is the end-of-day open interest?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the ETIRD workbook (pp.107-108), open interest is the total outstanding contracts with only one side counted; a trade where both sides open adds to OI, and a trade where one side closes against the other opening leaves OI unchanged. Here A buys new and B sells new — both open, adding 100. C sells to close against D buying new — no net effect. End-of-day OI = 5,000 + 100 = 5,100. The Trap: 5,050 mistakenly subtracts 50 for C's closing trade even though D replaces that position. 5,200 double-counts both sides of the A/B trade. 5,000 assumes no opening trades changed OI. Note: The rule: only count one side; opening + opening adds to OI, closing + opening is neutral, and closing + closing reduces OI.
